headline: Four Bets, Two Winners, And A Grand Total Of $2.59
paragraphs: Week 9 was less a slate than a rounding error. Four games graded, two waved off, two drew action, and four tickets went out at ten dollars apiece. The ledger closed 2-2 for a profit of 2.59 on 40 staked, a 6.5 percent ROI that would be thrilling if the absolute number were not roughly a vending machine transaction. The model expected 51.3 percent and hit 50. For once, calibrated.

The entire week was two games wearing four hats. Kennesaw State at Middle Tennessee went double green, the +2.5 spread and the +135 moneyline both cashing when Kennesaw State won 44-28 and made the 2.5 points decorative. The best call there was the moneyline, 6.2 probability points of edge for 13.50 back. The other game, Sam Houston at Missouri State, went double red. The model liked Sam Houston +190 at 42 percent and watched a 24-3 loss. Two plays, two tens, one lesson about correlation.

By market, the spread lost 0.91 and the moneyline made 3.50, which is the sort of split you only report because the table is right there. Of the three plays whose lines moved, exactly one moved toward the model, a 33.3 percent agreement rate the market should probably be proud of. Six real weeks in, the season sits 136-175-8 across 319 plays, down 413.91, minus 13 percent ROI, with a 43.7 percent win rate against an expectation of 60.1. That gap is the whole story.

There is also a hindsight week sitting off to the side, 66 plays, 40-25-1, up 110.47 at 16.7 percent ROI, graded with the benefit of already knowing how the games ended. It is excluded for a reason, and the reason is that picking winners after the fact is not a skill, it is reading. The real number is negative 413.91. Week 9 moved it by 2.59, which is to say it did not move it.
